text.p: Overnight rain delayed England's preparations for the second and final test as the net facilities at Harare Sports Club were unfit for a scheduled Christmas morning net session on Wednesday.
Rain also affected England's practice on Tuesday and with the forecast predicting more wet weather a draw could be a likely outcome.
The rain meant all-rounder Craig White was denied his chance to practice with England's squad following his arrival from Australia where he had been holidaying since the end of the England A tour.

He is match-fit following that two month tour, during which he took 16 wickets and scored 394 runs, but because of the rain now has only Thursday's planned practice session in which to convince England's management he is ready to be pitched straight into the second test.
However, England coach David Lloyd hinted strongly on Tuesday that White, called in as back-up for the injured Ronnie Irani, could be drafted into the test attack as a third seamer.

Meanwhile, Lloyd has been let off the hook by first test match referee Hanumant Singh. Lloyd was accused by a Zimbabwe cricket official of bad behaviour during the closing overs of the game in Bulawayo on Sunday.
A statement from Singh said that the matter had been dealt with amicably between the two parties and that no details would be revealed to the press.
The match ended in an exciting draw with the scores level but amid great frustration for England at Zimbabwe's wide bowling.
The second test is followed by two more one-day internationals on January 1 and 3 before England move on to tour New Zealand.
Zimbabwe: G.Flower, M.Dekker, A. Campbell (captain), D.Houghton, A. Flower, A.Waller, B. Strang, G. Whittall, P.Strang, H. Streak, H. Olonga, E. Brandes.
England: M.Atherton (captain), N.Knight, A. Stewart, N. Hussain, J. Crawley, G. Thorpe, D. Gough, R. Croft, A. Mullally, C. White, P. Tufnell, C. Silverwood, A. Caddick.
